newsitem.title: HONG KONG: COSCO Pac 1996 net seen higher.
newsitem.headline: COSCO Pac 1996 net seen higher.

text.p: COSCO Pacific Ltd is expected to report strong net profit growth for 1996 on the back of its growing container leasing business and the first full-year contribution of a container port unit, analysts said on Friday.
"The organic growth of its container leasing business should boost the profit figure," a Vickers Ballas analyst said.

The China-backed company, indirectly-controlled by the giant China Ocean Shipping (Group) Co (COSCO Beijing), will report its calendar 1996 earnings on Monday. It had net profit of US$46.36 million in 1995.
"The company has been adding containers very aggressively and this is the core business of the company," said Alan Kasket, an investment analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
COSCO Pacific bought 55,000 20-foot equivalent units (TEUs) in new containers last year, bringing its fleet to 351,000 TEUs by the end of 1996, Kasket said.
The company's container utilisation rate was high, probably around 95 percent compared to the industry average of about 80-82 percent, he added.
Kasket put the company's net profit in 1996 at US$86 million (HK$670 million) while Vickers' forecast for COSCO Pacific's 1996 net was HK$601 million.
The consensus forecast in Edinburgh Financial Publishing's Estimate Directory put the company's 1996 net at HK$561 million (US$72 million), up 55 percent from the previous year.
Container leasing is estimated to have accounted for about two-thirds of COSCO Pacific's profit in 1996, analysts said.
Strong demand from the parent company due to its purchase of new ships last year provided COSCO Pacific with a steady growth in container leasing, an analyst at European house said.
The company has said its parent had six container vessels with a capacity of 5,250 TEU each for delivery in late 1996 and 1997, which would benefit COSCO Pacific's leasing business.
COSCO Pacific could only meet 70 percent of COSCO Beijing's container demand in 1996, while COSCO Beijing accounted for over 90 percent of COSCO Pacific's turnover in 1995, it added.
The remaining one-third of COSCO Pacific's total profit is expected to come from its terminal operation and management business, mainly in the COSCO-HIT Terminals (HK) Ltd.
"The other major profit growth was from the full year contribution of its CT8 operation, which it bought in November, 1995," an analyst at a European house said.
COSCO Pacific bought a 50 percent stake in COSCO-HIT, which operates part of Container Terminal Eight (CT8) in Hong Kong's Kwai Chung, from COSCO Beijing.
Analysts also expected the company to announce its China port terminal acquisition plan soon.
COSCO Pacific said this week it was in talks to buy certain China port terminals from its parent, COSCO (Hong Kong) Group Ltd, the local investment arm of COSCO Beijing.
COSCO Pacific's target assets were most likely be in Qingdao, Zhangjiakou, Shanghai and Yantian, said Pamela Lam, an analyst at Pacific Challenge Securities Ltd.
"I expect COSCO Pacific will acquire the asset from its parent, COSCO Hong Kong at a P/E (price earnings) multiple of below 10 times," Lam said.
"If the company managed to buy the asset at or below 12 times P/E, it would enhance its profit," an analyst at a European house said.
